message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020:

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern twist on the classic horror tale, it blends psychological suspense with social commentary on abuse and gaslighting. |
| 2 | **Tenet** | Christopher Nolan | John David Washington, Robert Pattinson | Though more sci‑fi, its intricate time‑travel plot and high‑stakes espionage make it a cerebral crime‑thriller. |
| 3 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced dialogue and layered heist narrative keep viewers guessing. |
| 4 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Ewan McGregor, Sacha Baron Cohen | A courtroom drama that doubles as a political thriller, capturing the tension of the 1969 protest trial. |
| 5 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | A sprawling mob saga that uses de‑identified footage and deepfake tech to explore aging and regret. |
| 6 | **Uncut Gems** | Benny Safdie, Josh Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett | Sandler’s manic performance drives a tense, almost claustrophobic crime story about addiction and desperation. |
| 7 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A Danish thriller that examines paranoia and the consequences of false accusations. |
| 8 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily Sullivan, Daniel Lapaine | A gritty revenge story set in colonial Australia, blending historical context with visceral suspense. |
| 9 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval duel turned crime‑thriller, exploring truth, justice, and gender dynamics. |
|10 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A Spanish allegory that turns a vertical prison into a psychological thriller about class and survival. |

These films cover a range of sub‑genres—from psychological thrillers and heists to courtroom dramas and historical epics—while maintaining the core elements of tension, intrigue, and moral ambiguity that define the crime‑thriller genre.
